# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Categories by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*Games where the primary goal is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
Games where the loop may pass freely through any eligible cell

- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass through all circles; black/white circles impose different turn/straight constraints
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells and numbered arrow cells; arrows indicate black cell counts in a direction

### 1.2 Directional/Wind-Constrained Loop
Games where the direction of loop travel is governed by external forces or rules

- **Nagareru** — Loop direction constrained by wind arrows; cells with side-wind force lateral movement
- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must pass through all "Gates" in a specified order

### 1.3 Cell-Type Constrained Loop
Games where specific cell types impose strict rules on how the loop passes through them

- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through rooms exactly once; alternates between moon-rooms and sun-rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop passes through white circles; within each bold-line area, all circles are either all straight or all turning
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through all black circles with each circle as the exact midpoint of a straight segment

---

## 2. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*Games where the primary goal is to determine which cells to paint black (or a color)*

### 2.1 Connectivity-Rule Shading
Games where the shape or connectivity of shaded regions is the primary constraint

- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form one connected wall; white regions each contain exactly one number indicating their size; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Rooms contain specified numbers of black cells; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a straight line; no adjacent black cells
- **Hitori** — No number repeats in any row or column; black cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers indicate total white cells visible (horizontally + vertically) from that cell; black cells cannot touch; all white cells connected
- **Usowan** — Numbers indicate adjacent black cells, but exactly one number per bold-line region is deliberately wrong; no adjacent black cells; white cells stay connected

### 2.2 Shape-Constrained Shading
Games where shaded cells must form specific geometric shapes

- **Choco Banana** — Black cells must form rectangles/squares; white cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate region size
- **Kurotto** — Circled numbers indicate the sum of black cells extending orthogonally from the circle; cells with circles stay white
- **Norinori** — Each bold-line region contains exactly two black cells; black cells are placed in domino pairs (two connected cells)
- **Nuritwin** — Each region contains exactly two same-sized blocks of shaded cells; all shaded cells connected across regions; no 2×2 shaded squares

### 2.3 Tetromino/Polyomino Shading
Games where shaded cells must form specific polyomino shapes

- **LITS** — Each bold-line region contains one tetromino (L, I, T, or S); same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch orthogonally; all colored squares connected; no 2×2 colored squares

### 2.4 Hint-Directed Shading
Games where numerical clues along rows/columns guide shading

- **Tilepaint** — Diagonal-line cells provide counts of black cells rightward or downward; entire tiles (bold-line areas) are all black or all white; solution depicts an object
- **Sto-stone** — Rooms contain specified counts of black cells; when "dropped" downward, black cells fill exactly the bottom half of the grid

---

## 3. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*Games where the primary goal is to fill cells with numbers according to constraints*

### 3.1 Latin Square / Non-Repetition
Games built on the constraint that numbers cannot repeat in rows, columns, or regions

- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 block with no repetition

### 3.2 Region-Completion Number Fill
Games where numbers fill regions according to size or sequence rules

- **Fillomino** — Divide grid into blocks; each block filled with a number equal to its cell count; same-sized blocks cannot touch orthogonally
- **Ripple Effect** — Rooms contain consecutive numbers from 1; duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least that number's value of cells
- **Makaro** — Rooms contain 1 through (room size); arrow cells indicate which neighbor has the highest value; no same number in adjacent rooms

### 3.3 Sequence / Snake Number Placement
Games where numbers represent ordered sequences or positional values

- **Hebi** — Place 1–5 in white cells to form snakes (head to tail); snakes cannot touch each other; directional "vision" rules prevent snakes from seeing each other
- **Nansuke** — Fill blank cells with digits from a provided list; numbers read horizontally or vertically

---

## 4. REGION-DIVISION GAMES
*Games where the primary goal is to partition the grid into regions satisfying given constraints*

### 4.1 Rectangle/Square Division
Games where regions must be rectangular

- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count

### 4.2 Polyomino Division
Games where regions must be specific polyomino shapes or sizes

- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each); numbers indicate how many block-boundary lines surround that cell
- **Sashigane** — Divide grid into L-shaped blocks (one cell wide); circles mark the bend; arrows point toward the bend; numbers indicate block size

### 4.3 Paired / Symmetric Division
Games where each region must contain two congruent sub-regions

- **Double Choco** — Each block contains a white sub-region and a gray sub-region of identical shape (rotation/reflection allowed); numbers indicate sub-region size

---

## 5. OBJECT/PIECE PLACEMENT GAMES
*Games where discrete objects or symbols are placed into the grid*

### 5.1 Light / Illumination Placement
Games based on placing items that "illuminate" cells

- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other

### 5.2 Triangle / Symbol Placement
Games where geometric symbols are placed to satisfy shape constraints

- **Shakashaka** — Place right-triangle halves in cells; remaining white areas must form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate adjacent triangle count

### 5.3 Block / Domino Placement
Games where pre-defined blocks or pieces are placed

- **Chained Block** — Fill cells to form numbered blocks; blocks touch only at corners (forming chains); no two same-shaped blocks in one chain; each block contains one number or "?"

---

## 6. PATH / CONNECTION GAMES
*Games where elements must be connected or paths must be drawn between specific points*

### 6.1 Island Bridge Connection
Games where numbered nodes must be connected by bridges

- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges equal to the island's number; max two bridges between any pair; bridges cannot cross; all islands connected

### 6.2 Pair Connection
Games where matching numbers or symbols must be linked

- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines that fill the grid

### 6.3 Sequential Block Connection (Evolving Path)
Games where connected groups must grow sequentially

- **Evolomino** — Place squares in white cells; groups of connected squares form blocks; each arrow defines a sequence of blocks where each successive block adds exactly one cell to the previous shape

---

## 7. MOVEMENT / MIGRATION GAMES
*Games where existing elements are moved to satisfy placement constraints*

### 7.1 Circle/Token Migration
Games where circles or tokens slide to target zones

- **Satogaeri** — Move circles horizontally or vertically into their home country (one circle per country); numbered circles move exactly that many cells; paths cannot cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; gray area numbers must equal the sum of circles entering; arrow paths cannot cross or bend

---

## 8. HYBRID / COMPOSITE GAMES
*Games combining two or more major mechanics (e.g., shading + loop, or division + number placement)*

### 8.1 Shading + Maze/Path
Games that combine cell shading with a navigable path

- **Nurimeizu** — Paint rooms to create walls; white cells form a maze from S to G; all circles on shortest path; all triangles off shortest path; no 2×2 uniform squares

### 8.2 Symbol Fill + Territorial Rules
Games that fill cells with directional symbols under regional constraints

- **Juosan** — Fill each cell with — or |; territories have counts specifying excess of one symbol; — cannot extend more than two cells vertically; | cannot extend more than two cells horizontally

### 8.3 Shading + Promontory Shape
Games combining shading with strict white-cell shape constraints

- **Nurimisaki** — Circle cells are "Misaki" (promontories) with exactly one white neighbor; numbers indicate white cell run length; all white cells connected; no 2×2 uniform squares

### 8.4 Loop + Shading
Games where both a loop and black-cell placement must be determined together

- **Yajilin** *(also listed under Loop)* — Arrow/number cells reveal black cell counts; loop avoids black and numbered cells; black cells cannot touch orthogonally

### 8.5 Drawing + Sequential Block Growth
Games combining path-drawing with evolving piece shapes

- **Pencils** — Identify pencil bodies (straight runs of cells) and draw lines from their tips; line length equals number in pencil; lines cannot cross or branch

---

## Summary Structural Overview

```
Grid-Based Logic Games
│
├── 1. Loop-Drawing Games
│   ├── 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop (Slitherlink, Masyu, Yajilin)
│   ├── 1.2 Directional/Wind-Constrained Loop (Nagareru, Suraromu)
│   └── 1.3 Cell-Type Constrained Loop (Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop)
│
├── 2. Cell-Shading / Painting Games
│   ├── 2.1 Connectivity-Rule Shading (Nurikabe, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Usowan)
│   ├── 2.2 Shape-Constrained Shading (Choco Banana, Kurotto, Norinori, Nuritwin)
│   ├── 2.3 Tetromino/Polyomino Shading (LITS)
│   └── 2.4 Hint-Directed Shading (Tilepaint, Sto-stone)
│
├── 3. Number-Placement Games
│   ├── 3.1 Latin Square / Non-Repetition (Sudoku)
│   ├── 3.2 Region-Completion Number Fill (Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro)
│   └── 3.3 Sequence / Snake Number Placement (Hebi, Nansuke)
│
├── 4. Region-Division Games
│   ├── 4.1 Rectangle/Square Division (Shikaku)
│   ├── 4.2 Polyomino Division (Five Cells, Sashigane)
│   └── 4.3 Paired / Symmetric Division (Double Choco)
│
├── 5. Object/Piece Placement Games
│   ├── 5.1 Light / Illumination Placement (Akari)
│   ├── 5.2 Triangle / Symbol Placement (Shakashaka)
│   └── 5.3 Block / Domino Placement (Chained Block)
│
├── 6. Path / Connection Games
│   ├── 6.1 Island Bridge Connection (Hashiwokakero)
│   ├── 6.2 Pair Connection (Numberlink)
│   └── 6.3 Sequential Block Connection (Evolomino)
│
├── 7. Movement / Migration Games
│   └── 7.1 Circle/Token Migration (Satogaeri, Yosenabe)
│
└── 8. Hybrid / Composite Games
    ├── 8.1 Shading + Maze/Path (Nurimeizu)
    ├── 8.2 Symbol Fill + Territorial Rules (Juosan)
    ├── 8.3 Shading + Promontory Shape (Nurimisaki)
    ├── 8.4 Loop + Shading (Yajilin)
    └── 8.5 Drawing + Sequential Block Growth (Pencils)
```
